question: Where in a human body can anaerobic respiration take place?

options.text: Only in red blood cells in the veins

solution:
The correct answer is __**In the cytoplasm of cells**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Anaerobic **respiration takes place in the cytoplasm of cells in the human body. **

 
 
• It is the** release of a relatively small amount of energy in cells by the breakdown of food substances in the absence of oxygen.**
 
• **Anaerobic respiration happens in muscles during hard exercise.**
 
• The cytoplasm is the jelly-like substance that fills the space between the nucleus and the plasma membrane
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Anaerobic respiration** is the type of respiration through which cells can break down sugars to generate energy in the absence of oxygen.

 
 
• This is in contrast to the highly efficient process of aerobic respiration, which relies on oxygen to produce energy.
 
 
 
• **Aerobic respiration** is the process by which organisms use oxygen to burn fuel, such as fats and sugars, into chemical energy.
 
 
• In contrast, anaerobic respiration does not use oxygen.
 
• Respiration is used by all cells to turn fuel into energy that can be used to power cellular processes.
